Q4858573.label: 1981 Barbadian general election
Q4858573.summary: General elections were held in Barbados on 18 June 1981. The result was a victory for the ruling Barbados Labour Party, which won 17 of the 27 seats. Voter turnout was 71.6%.

Q5614285.label: 1990 Guatemalan general election
Q5614285.summary: General elections were held in Guatemala on 11 November 1990. with a second round of the presidential election held on 6 January 1991. The presidential election resulted in a victory for Jorge Serrano Elías of the Solidarity Action Movement, whilst the National Centre Union won the Congressional elections.

Q1511117.label: 1995 Portuguese legislative election
Q1511117.summary: The 1995 Portuguese legislative election took place on 1 October. The election renewed all 230 members of the Assembly of the Republic.

Q1221325.label: Hungarian European Union membership referendum, 2003
Q1221325.summary: A referendum on joining the European Union was held in Hungary on 12 April 2003. The proposal was approved by 84% of voters, with a voter turnout of 46%. Hungary subsequently joined the EU on 1 May 2004.

Q1773261.label: 2003 Serbian parliamentary election
Q1773261.desc: 2003 election for the parliament of Serbia
Q1773261.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Serbia on 28 December 2003 to elect members of the National Assembly.

Q705229.label: Dragan Mikerević
Q705229.summary: Dragan Mikerević is a Bosnian Serb politician who served as Prime Minister of Republika Srpska from 2003 to 2005. Previously, he served as Chairman of the Council of Ministers of Bosnia and Herzegovina from March to December 2002.

Q1582285.label: 1964 Swedish general election
Q1582285.summary: General elections were held in Sweden on 20 September 1964. The Swedish Social Democratic Party remained the largest party, winning 113 of the 233 seats in the Andra kammaren of the Riksdag. Tage Erlander's Social Democratic government was returned to power.

Q2035405.label: 1995 Icelandic parliamentary election
Q2035405.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Iceland on 8 April 1995. They were the first elections after the Althing became a unicameral parliament in 1991. The Independence Party remained the largest party, winning 25 of the 63 seats.

Q3045069.label: Icelandic loan guarantees referendum
Q3045069.desc: Referendum held in Iceland on 6 March 2010
Q3045069.summary: The 2010 Icesave referendum, was held in Iceland on 6 March 2010.

Q16241869.label: Sino-Portuguese Joint Declaration
aliases: Joint Declaration on the Question of Macau
Q16241869.summary: The Joint Declaration on the Question of Macau, or Sino-Portuguese Joint Declaration, was a treaty between Portugal and the People's Republic of China over the status of Macau. The full name of the treaty is Joint Declaration of the Government of the Portuguese Republic and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the question of Macau.

mentions.c: International: Treaty signed: Sino-Portuguese Joint Declaration

Q757965.label: assassination of Rafic Hariri
Q757965.summary: On 14 February 2005, former Prime Minister of Lebanon Rafic Hariri was assassinated along with 21 others in an explosion in Beirut, Lebanon. Explosives equivalent to around 1,000 kilograms of TNT were detonated as his motorcade drove near the St. George Hotel.

mentions.c: Lebanon: Assassination: assassination of Rafic Hariri

Q111383245.label: Battle of Avdiivka
Q111383245.desc: 2022–2024 military engagement during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
Q111383245.summary: The Battle of Avdiivka was a major battle between the Russian and Ukrainian Armed Forces for control of Avdiivka, a city in Donetsk Oblast, during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present).

mentions.c: Part of Russian invasion of Ukraine

Q4871373.label: Battle of Kamalpur
Q4871373.desc: 1971 battle of the Bangladesh Liberation War
Q4871373.summary: The Battle of Kamalpur, is one of the most significant military engagements fought by the Mukti Bahini in 1971 during its war of independence from Pakistan. The Pakistan Army set up a military camp at Kamalpur which was attacked by 1st East Bengal Regiment of Z Force several times. The first attack was made on June 12, and a second attack was made on July 31, 1971, also another attack at 22 October 1971 and in total, there were 18 battles in Kamalpur.

Q25425613.label: Kulchabat, Bala Karz and Mushkizi massacre
Q25425613.desc: war crime perpetrated by the Red Army
Q25425613.wiki: Kulchabat, Bala Karz and Mushkizi massacre
Q25425613.summary: The Kulchabat, Bala Karz and Mushkizi massacre was an alleged war crime reportedly perpetrated by the Soviet Army on 12 October 1983 in the villages of Kulchabat, Bala Karz and Mushkizi in the Kandahar Province, Afghanistan, during the Soviet–Afghan War. Reports indicate that up to 360 people were gathered at the three village squares and shot, including 20 girls and over a dozen older people.

Q4870861.label: Battle of Delft
Q4870861.summary: The Battle of Delft was a naval battle on December 25, 2007 and part of the Sri Lankan Civil War. The Sri Lankan Navy claimed that it received reports of a boat cluster moving off of Delft Island. After moving in to investigate clashes erupted and fierce sea battle ensued. Both sides claimed victory. The pro-rebel Tamilnet claimed that the Sea Tigers sank one Sri Lankan Navy vessel and the Sri Lankan Navy suffered 10 casualties. However, the Sri Lankan Defense ministry claimed that six Tiger boats were sunk and over 40 Tigers were killed.

mentions.c: Part of Sri Lankan Civil War

Q1518797.label: Operation Karez
Q1518797.summary: Operation Karez was a military operation between May 13–23, 2008 involving Norwegian and German ISAF and Afghan government forces against the Taliban as part of the war in Afghanistan. Their objective was to eliminate the presence of Taliban insurgents who had regrouped in the area in the aftermath of Operation Harekate Yolo in late 2007.

Q192717.label: streptomycin
Q192717.summary: Streptomycin is an antibiotic medication used to treat a number of bacterial infections, including tuberculosis, Mycobacterium avium complex, endocarditis, brucellosis, Burkholderia infection, plague, tularemia, and rat bite fever. For active tuberculosis it is often given together with isoniazid, rifampicin, and pyrazinamide. It is administered by injection into a vein or muscle.

Q1680589.label: Reform Party of Canada
Q1680589.summary: The Reform Party of Canada was a right-wing populist and conservative federal political party in Canada that existed from 1987 to 2000. Reform was founded as a Western Canada-based protest movement that eventually became a populist conservative party, with strong social conservative and fiscal conservative elements. It was initially motivated by profound Western Canadian discontent with the Progressive Conservative Party government of Brian Mulroney.

Q383693.label: Fatherland League
Q383693.summary: The Fatherland League was a Norwegian nationalist and conservative political organisation during the interwar period. Founded in 1925, the movement aimed to unite all bourgeois forces against the rise of the Labour Party. At its peak of popular support and political influence around 1930, it was the single largest mass movement ever organised on the political right in Norway, with an estimated 100,000 members. The movement began to decline through the 1930s, followed by some unsuccessful attempts to gain direct influence as a political party.

Q717.label: Venezuela
Q717.summary: Venezuela, officially the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, is a country on the northern coast of South America, consisting of a continental landmass and various islands and islets in the Caribbean Sea. It comprises an area of 912,050 km2 (352,140 sq mi), with a population estimated at 31.8 million in 2025. The capital and largest urban agglomeration is Caracas. The continental territory is bordered on the north by the Caribbean Sea and the Atlantic Ocean, on the west by Colombia, on the south by Brazil, on the east by Guyana, and on the northeast by Trinidad and Tobago.
